## 0.5.8

- Quit, updates and Settings close continue if a pending History deletion cannot finish. Closing also stops new deletion requests, while undone rows stay saved.
- Rapid appearance choices keep the latest selection without replaying earlier saves. Mode appears in search only for Paper, Glass and Soft.
- The cloud cleanup privacy line explains when Rewrite can use Groq and when a key or mode change is needed.

- Settings groups related controls into six searchable pages, with advanced options folded away. Cloud cleanup opens key setup when no key is saved, and the meeting-key and Dictionary-sharing labels say what they control.
- Paper, Glass and Soft offer Light, Dark and Match Windows appearances, including setup, dictation and problem reports. Dark controls keep clear outlines with quieter row dividers, raised deletion notices with distinct Undo buttons and warm Paper selections.
- Deleting a History row offers Undo for six seconds. Clear All still asks first.

- Paper, Glass and Soft use more consistent page spacing, compact Dictionary and Learning forms, clearer theme pickers and accent-colored listening meters. Setup and problem reports have simpler spacing and clearer text.
- Full cleanup can split long chat and AI dictations into idea paragraphs, keeps kind of and sort of, and asks for conservative filler, compound and restart cleanup. Built-in terminals, editors and apps saved as Code and terminal stay one block, while other apps keep their existing paragraph handling.

- Editing a title while speaker data is damaged keeps the names for the repair notice. Call names cannot be changed until the speaker data is repaired.

- Saving a title or name cannot put old names back after a speaker rerun. Damaged speaker recovery records keep the meeting visible with a repair offer and a byte-preserving backup; unproved names stay hidden.
- Speaker requests wait behind the current run, with one queued rerun per meeting. A newly finished call waits only for its own separation before its automatic summary, and an automatic failure leaves the retry offer without an error.
- Short microphone losses appear in the meeting transcript with a minimum duration. During recording, these marks stay visible as more audio is lost.

- Damaged speaker data can be separated again while the audio is kept, with one backup and unproved names under Names not kept. Old speaker confirmations stay unconfirmed after recovery.

- Report a problem can use a Dicta relay when one is configured. Review your description, app version, platform and optional log of safe event names and error kinds before sending; logs start off, and reports stay unavailable until a relay is deployed and configured.

- An old owner confirmation cannot confirm a reused speaker label after separation changes. The page reloads with a muted notice below the title, and save failures say the confirmation could not be saved.

- Meeting decoding waits for the Dicta key to be classified, so a delayed dictation stays private and an ignored press keeps public speech. After 30 seconds without a decision, only that press's span is omitted; audio saving stays immediate.
- If the app closes before a Dicta key press is classified, recovery omits only its undecided audio range with the existing privacy notice. A note whose audio was erased after the 30-second limit is shown as not saved.
- Meeting privacy diagnostics count late dictation and held-note reports only while capture is live, record report ages, measure decoding holds from segmentation, and count retracted lines without recording content.

- Failed private-audio erasures retry at most once a second during recording, and again at Stop and recovery. The meeting promises a retry only while recovery is available; playback and transcripts keep the pending audio hidden.

- You can try separating speakers from kept in-person audio; the page explains the shared-mic limit. A one-voice result keeps Room and its name, while a split uses unnamed speakers and lists names it could not keep.
